{{short description|Pioneering Swedish Air Force trainee}}
[[File:Inger-lena-hultberg.jpg|thumb|Inger-lena-hultberg]]

'''Inger-Lena Lamm''', née '''Hultberg''' (born 27 December 1942) is considered to be the first woman in Sweden who volunteered for an education designed for those entering military service.<ref name=forsvar>{{cite web|url=http://www.forsvarsmakten.se/sv/information-och-fakta/var-historia/artiklar/inger-lena-hultberg/|title=Inger-Lena Hultberg: Sveriges första kvinnliga värnpliktige|publisher=[[Swedish Armed Forces]] |accessdate=15 December 2016 |language=sv}}</ref><ref name=lth>{{cite web|url=https://www.lth.se/fileadmin/lth/omlth/kommunikation/lthnytt/LTH_Nytt_01_2010.pdf|title=Inger-Lena - Första trulan vid LTH|publisher=[[Faculty of Engineering (LTH), Lund University]]|accessdate=15 December 2016 |language=sv}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born and raised in [[Lund]], Hultberg's father was a teacher and her mother, literary historian. She showed an interest in technology from an early age, specializing in maths at high school and working on a special project in [[aerodynamics]]. She was always interested in the family's car and motorcycles. While studying English in England, she spent her free time observing the planes at [[Croydon Airport]] and [[Biggin Hill]], famous for its wartime activities. Her first flight was in Sweden in an old two-seater [[North American T-6 Texan|SK 16]].<ref name=forsvar/>

She then embarked on a course in physics at the [[Faculty of Engineering (LTH), Lund University|Faculty of Engineering]] at the [[Lund University]]. In the summer vacation of 1962, she was the first woman to be admitted to the [[Royal Swedish Air Force Materiel Administration]]'s workshop school in [[Västerås]] where she spent most of her time in the {{ill|Swedish Air Force Maintenance Depot at Arboga|lt=Swedish Air Force Maintenance Depot|sv|Centrala Flygverkstaden Arboga}} at [[Arboga]] training as a flight engineer. The only woman in a group of 30, she returned to the Air Force school for the summers of 1963 and 1964 qualifying as a flight engineer. But she realized she would never be admitted to serve in the Air Force. As a result, she decided to continue her academic studies, eventually graduating from Lund in mathematical physics.<ref name=forsvar/><ref name=lth/>

Hultberg subsequently was employed as a physicist at the [[Lund University Hospital]] until her retirement in 2010.<ref name=lth/>
